mechanism: Fluctuating selection through time maintains multiple morphs locally
primary_prediction: C-only/C+S should have greater interannual or flowering-season environmental turnover than S-only
evidence_type_needed: independent temporal environmental data at fixed occupied locations
current_test: Static BIO4 candidate only; real dynamic TerraClimate protocol frozen but not executed
current_result: BIO4 direction favours C but weakens after mean-temperature/latitude controls; no dynamic result claimed
literature_anchor: Sapir et al. 2021, doi:10.1016/j.tree.2021.01.011; Gentiana leucomelaena 10.1002/ece3.2899

mechanism: Anthocyanin-linked stress tolerance changes morph fitness independently of pollinators
primary_prediction: Spatially structured stress should favour S; temporally variable stress may favour C
evidence_type_needed: soil chemistry, drought/UV/temperature stress, ideally morph-specific fitness
current_test: Static climate breadth/heterogeneity; same-literature abiotic examples
current_result: Macroclimatic breadth/heterogeneity null; Leptosiphon provides a strong soil/drought/UV association but comparative edaphic test is pending
literature_anchor: Leptosiphon parviflorus 10.1002/ajb2.70018; Sapir et al. 2017 PMID 28430395

mechanism: Spatially divergent selection sorts morphs among populations
primary_prediction: S-only/C+S should show stronger population-specific environmental or reciprocal-fitness divergence than C-only
evidence_type_needed: independent soil/climate/population-environment contrasts or reciprocal-transplant evidence
current_test: Same-literature direct-evidence screen plus independent macroclimate spatial-structure screen
current_result: Direct local-adaptation evidence: S 3/7 vs C 0/11, Fisher p=0.0429; same-literature ascertainment prevents confirmatory use. Independent spatial climate structure metrics were null.
literature_anchor: Disa porrecta 10.1093/aob/mcaf074; Eruca sativa 10.1093/jisesa/iez038; Linanthus parryae reciprocal-transplant literature

mechanism: Different pollinator guilds or preferences dominate in different regions
primary_prediction: S-only/C+S should show stronger geographic turnover in pollinator guild composition/preferences
evidence_type_needed: independent plant-pollinator interaction data across the species range
current_result: Direct geographic pollinator-mosaic evidence: S 2/7 vs C 0/11, Fisher p=0.1373
literature_anchor: Disa porrecta 10.1093/aob/mcaf074; Eruca sativa 10.1093/jisesa/iez038; Trunschke et al. 2021 doi:10.3389/fpls.2021.617851

mechanism: Multiple pollinator guilds or selective agents favour different morphs in the same population
primary_prediction: C-only/C+S should have more opposing within-population selection regimes than S-only
evidence_type_needed: morph-specific visitation/fitness by multiple agents measured in the same populations
current_result: Strong examples exist (e.g. Raphanus seasonal bee/syrphid preferences), but comparative sample is too small
literature_anchor: Sapir et al. 2021 doi:10.1016/j.tree.2021.01.011; Raphanus sativus 10.2307/2444019

mechanism: Autonomous selfing rescues a morph disadvantaged under pollinator-mediated selection
primary_prediction: C-only/C+S should show higher autonomous selfing/autofertility than S-only
evidence_type_needed: autofertility or spontaneous selfing, not self-compatibility alone
current_test: Manual breeding-system audit; global SC/SI database sensitivity
current_result: SC vs SI itself null (complete-case Fisher p≈1.0). Broad autonomous-selfing evidence C 4/7 vs S 0/6, p=0.0699; strict direct subset 3/6 vs S 0/6, p=0.1818.
literature_anchor: Silene littorea 10.1111/plb.13209; Sapir et al. 2017 review PMID 28430395

mechanism: Morphs differ in flowering time and therefore experience different pollinators or abiotic regimes
primary_prediction: Within-population phenological differences can stabilize C; geographic phenological turnover can contribute to S
evidence_type_needed: morph-specific flowering phenology and pollinator/climate histories
current_test: Same-literature examples only; dynamic climate protocol does not yet include morph-specific phenology
current_result: Gentiana provides a strong within-population temporal example; comparative test pending

mechanism: Gene flow homogenizes nearby populations whereas restricted connectivity permits spatial sorting
primary_prediction: Higher functional connectivity should favour C; lower gene flow/connectivity should favour S
evidence_type_needed: population-genetic connectivity, dispersal kernels, or defensible landscape resistance
current_result: Range size and GBIF fragmentation proxies did not discriminate C/S; these are not gene-flow measurements
literature_anchor: Sapir et al. 2017 review PMID 28430395; Ipomoea purpurea population-genetic literature

mechanism: Opposing pollinator and herbivore/florivore selection prevents fixation
primary_prediction: C-only/C+S should be enriched for documented opposing biotic selection
evidence_type_needed: independent or experimental morph-specific pollination and herbivory fitness components
current_result: Clear focal example in Raphanus; direct herbivory evidence broadly C 2/11 vs S 0/7, Fisher p=0.4967

mechanism: Dormancy stores morphs across years and converts temporal fitness reversals into stable local coexistence
primary_prediction: C-only/C+S should have stronger seed-bank persistence/dormancy where temporal selection fluctuates
evidence_type_needed: seed-bank longevity/persistence or germination fraction data
current_test: No adequate global cross-species data linked yet
literature_anchor: Linanthus parryae fluctuating-selection literature; storage-effect theory

mechanism: Founder events or drift generate spatially patchy morph frequencies without current adaptive sorting
primary_prediction: S should associate with low effective population size, isolation, or neutral genetic structure unexplained by environment
evidence_type_needed: neutral population-genetic structure and demographic history
current_result: Species-level examples exist but no comparative test

primary_prediction: C-only/C+S should have greater clonality/persistence than S-only
evidence_type_needed: global clonality or clonal persistence traits with balanced coverage
current_result: Only 4/18 pure-state species covered; C 1/2 clonal vs S 1/2, Fisher p=1.0. Missing values not coded non-clonal.
